equity_bridge.note: 10-Q Q3-2026 Note 15: 2018-2020 NOPAs propose +2,073 of US taxable income (233.5 election + 625.3/530.7/683.6 transfer pricing) = ~435 of tax at 21% plus 153.0 of 40% penalties, before interest and before correlative Swiss relief; 2015-2017 NOD of 269.3 is already covered by 380.1 of advance payments (cash out the door, refund claim pending); 2021-2026 remain open on the same positions. Gross exposure if the IRS prevails everywhere is plausibly $1.5-2.0B; -450 is a ~30% probability-weighted view net of Swiss correlative adjustments. Bear-case tax path separately carries the forward-rate consequence.

historical_growth.basis: Continuing operations, FY2022 -> FY2025 for 3-year CAGRs. 5-year CAGRs (FY2020 -> FY2025) are on the reported basis, which includes Critical Care in FY2020-FY2024 and the COVID-depressed FY2020 trough, and are shown for completeness only.
historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2022 973.6-126.8-35.5; FY2023 642.8-139.4-67.2 (inventory build 289 and 109.9 Medtronic prepaid royalty); FY2024 289.9-162.3-120.3 (cash taxes on the Critical Care gain); FY2025 1,335.0-158.1-168.8. FY2020 interest income is not in the extracted set and is estimated at ~10 for the 5-year figure (immaterial to the CAGR).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (continuing ops, 10.8%) tempered toward the FY2026 guide (~11.5%) decelerating; used as the FY2027 base-case growth. Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor: it is inflated by the $3.3B Critical Care gain, not by retained operating earnings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 21.2% vs revenue 10.8% (>30% divergence) -- caused by the Sep-2024 Critical Care disposal gain (net income 4,174.6 in FY2024). GAAP EPS 3yr CAGR is negative because FY2025 absorbed 325.4 of IP litigation and 186.9 of impairments; adjusted EPS grew from ~2.50 (FY2022) to a guided 2.97-3.05 (FY2026). Neither EPS nor equity is a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (7.5%) is materially below reported FCF CAGR (11.1%). The gap is interest income, not SBC: interest income grew 35.5 -> 168.8 as the Critical Care proceeds were invested, and that income is stripped because the cash pile is added back in the bridge. SBC held at ~2.6% of revenue throughout.

scenario_narratives.base: Edwards remains the ~60%+ TAVR share leader in a market growing high-single digits on indication expansion (asymptomatic AS, Sep-2026 CMS NCD) and international penetration, while TMTT scales toward ~$1.6B by 2030 and turns profitable. Revenue growth decelerates from 9.5% to 3.5% over ten years; the owner-FCF margin builds from ~19% to ~23% as TMTT losses fade, partly offset by the 2032 Swiss incentive expiry. The IRS dispute is carried at a ~$450M expected cost in the equity bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: PROGRESS (moderate AS) approval plus asymptomatic coverage sustains TAVR at 9-10% through 2031, TMTT hits $2B by 2030 with the only complete mitral/tricuspid portfolio, EBITDA margin reaches 37%, and the cash tax rate stays near 20%.
scenario_narratives.bear: TAVR maturation and share loss to Evolut, hospital-capacity limits, and Abbott holding the repair market cap growth at 7% fading to 2%; margins stall at 32% under recurring litigation and impairments; the IRS wins the transfer-pricing method and the forward cash tax rate rises to 24%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on continuing operations with SBC fully expensed and the interest on the $4.6B cash-and-investments pile stripped (it is added back in the bridge). A 10-year horizon lets the TMTT ramp mature before capitalising; the terminal multiple is capped at 20x. Recurring IP litigation and external-innovation outflows are treated as a cost of the franchise (1.5pp margin haircut), not as one-offs. The IRS transfer-pricing exposure is carried as an explicit expected-value deduction so the headline value is after the tax tail, not before it.
key_risks_to_valuation: TAVR (74% of sales) growth decelerating faster than modelled as the US/EU market matures and Medtronic's Evolut takes share; each 1pp of sustained TAVR growth is ~0.75pp of group growth

IRS transfer-pricing dispute: 2018-2020 NOPAs alone propose ~$2.07B of extra US taxable income plus 40% penalties, with 2021-2026 open on the same positions; a full loss could exceed the $450M bridge by $1B+ and lift the forward cash tax rate
TMTT $1.5-2.0B 2030 target depends on trial readouts (CLASP IIF, ENCIRCLE) and on winning the repair market from Abbott; the base case already assumes ~$1.6B
Hospital cath-lab capacity and staffing constraints, the proximate cause of the July-2024 31% single-day fall
Reimbursement/CMS NCD policy and GPO pricing pressure on premium-priced devices; EU MDR/Swiss MRA supply-chain friction
Recurring impairments on minority stakes and options ($147M, $220M, $164M in 2025-26) and continued IP litigation cost; antitrust limits on bolt-on M&A after the FTC blocked JenaValve
Swiss tax incentive expiry in 2032 (~5pp of effective rate) is modelled; a faster unwind or US tax-law change is not

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of (regular Friday close); 52-week range 74.66-104.17
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via EW_Metrics.csv (105 periods FY2007-Q3 2026); 10-K FY2025 (income statement, cash flow statement, income-taxes-paid table, EPS note, investments note) and 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet 2026-09-30, cash flow statement, EPS table, Note 5 investments, Note 15 income taxes) in research/EW/Extracted/
data_sources.qualitative: EW_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): segment mix, FY2026 guidance from the 4 Nov 2026 Q3 call (sales ~+11.5%, adjusted EPS $2.97-3.05, TAVR 9-9.5%, TMTT $780-790M, adjusted operating margin high end of 28-29%, capex ~$280M), IRS NOPAs, FTC/JenaValve, CMS NCD

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E: 9M-2026 actual 5,105.1 (10-Q Q3-2026) plus Q4 of ~1,685 inside the guided $1.67-1.75B range (below midpoint for the ~$15M FX headwind); ~11.9% growth vs FY2025 6,067.6, consistent with the 'approximately 11.5%' raised guide of 4 Nov 2026.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares for Q3 2026 (10-Q EPS table: basic 576.3, diluted 577.6). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. Edwards is an active repurchaser (TTM 754.6 of buybacks incl. tax-withholding shares), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and equivalents 3,110.8 + short-term investments 1,533.9 (AFS commercial paper, treasuries, corporate debt, all due within 1 year) at 2026-09-30. Long-term investments (262.6: 39.0 bank deposits + 221.8 equity stakes in early-stage structural-heart companies) excluded -- the equity stakes were impaired 146.9 (2025) and 163.6 (9M-2026) and are not cash-like.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to Q3-2026 cash-flow add-back: FY2025 158.1 (10-K FY2025 line 3469) - 9M-2025 118.9 + 9M-2026 133.6 (10-Q Q3-2026 line 2023). Edwards publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure; shares withheld for employee taxes are settled inside the 'Purchases of treasury stock' line (10-K FY2025 line 5086), so no separate equity-tax add-on exists to include.
inputs.interest_income_note: TTM gross interest income: FY2025 168.8 (10-K income statement) - 9M-2025 (112.5 net + ~15 interest expense) + 9M-2026 (100.0 net + ~15). Interest expense on the 4.3% 2028 notes is ~20/yr; the 10-Q nets it inside 'Interest income, net'. Stripped because net cash (4,046) is ~3.7x the owner-FCF base. After-tax interest expense (~16/yr) is NOT added back, a ~1.5% conservative omission.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM OCF 1,716.9 (FY2025 1,595.2 - 9M-2025 1,144.3 + 9M-2026 1,266.0) less TTM capex 292.8 (260.2 - 162.8 + 195.4). TTM cash taxes are light (~230 vs a normalised ~360) because of a +97.7 income-tax-payable build in 9M-2026, while working capital absorbed ~354 in 9M-2026; the two roughly offset, so TTM owner FCF of 1,095 (16.4% of TTM revenue 6,675) is taken as the FY2026E base without further normalisation.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM purchases of treasury stock: FY2025 893.4 - 9M-2025 852.8 + 9M-2026 714.0. $1.5B programme authorised Sep-2025, ~$1.3B remaining at Q3-2026; cash actually spent is what is recorded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 for a defensive large-cap medtech (procedures are non-elective) gives a cost of equity ~9.2%; the capital structure is net cash with $600M of 4.3% notes, so WACC is effectively the cost of equity, rounded down to 8.5% for a franchise with 15 years of trial evidence and ~60%+ TAVR share. Held identical across scenarios -- risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842; total lease liabilities 107.1 at FY2025) are expensed inside opex, so the lease cost already sits inside the EBITDA margin path. Lease liabilities are therefore NOT added to net debt and lease_cost_pct_path is omitted (treatment A: lease in the flows, not in the bridge).
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is immaterial and loss-making (net loss attributable to NCI -4.1 FY2025, -6.6 9M-2026); the remaining NCI in the one consolidated VIE was bought out for 233.7 in 2025. Flows are taken as consolidated with no NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, US, capital-light implantable devices). 10-year explicit horizon because the TMTT platform (11.5% of FY2026E sales, growing 45%) is still loss-making/sub-scale and the owner-FCF margin is still ramping in year 5. BASIS: continuing operations only. Critical Care (834.9 of FY2021 revenue) was sold to BD in Sep-2024 and a small non-core surgical product group in Dec-2025, so FY2021 and earlier are not comparable; historical CAGRs are computed FY2022 -> FY2025. FY2024 owner FCF is ~0 because the cash taxes on the $3.3B Critical Care gain (1,196 cash taxes) flowed through OCF -- a one-off, not an operating signal. EBITDA MARGIN BUILD: FY2026 adjusted operating margin is guided to the high end of 28-29% (Q3-2026 alone 30.3%), and Edwards' adjusted figures do NOT add back SBC, so adjusted EBITDA pre-SBC = ~29.0 + SBC 2.55 + D&A 2.5 = ~34.0% of revenue. The driver path starts 1.5pp below that (32.5%) to carry a normalised charge for recurring IP litigation/settlements (325.4 in 2025, 40.4 in 2024, 203.5 in 2023 -- ~3% of revenue on average) and for the external-innovation outflows (options, notes receivable, minority stakes: ~230 in FY2025, 73 in 9M-2026) that sit in investing activities outside capex and are repeatedly impaired. CASH TAX: adjusted ETR ~16-17% today; path starts at 18% and ramps to 21-22% because the Swiss tax incentive expires in 2032 (worth 93.9 in 2025, ~0.16/share) and because the IRS transfer-pricing position, if lost, moves royalty income into the US. The $174.4M California R&D-credit valuation allowance (9M-2026) is non-cash and excluded. IRS DISPUTE: carried as an equity-bridge deduction (see equity_bridge) rather than in the flows. Y1 (FY2027) base owner-FCF margin builds to ~19% vs TTM 16.4%: the gap is the normalised-litigation and working-capital assumptions replacing a TTM that carried a 325 settlement year and a 354 working-capital absorption. Hurdle entry price uses the house 15%.

bear.narrative: A repeat of July 2024: hospital cath-lab capacity and staffing cap procedure growth, Medtronic's Evolut (3-year SMART data) takes more than a 'slight' share, and GPO/CMS pricing pressure arrives, so TAVR settles at 3-4% by 2029; TMTT reaches only ~$1.2B by 2030 as Abbott's TriClip/MitraClip hold the repair market and trial readouts (CLASP IIF, ENCIRCLE) disappoint; the EBITDA margin stalls at 32% under continued IP litigation and impairments on the minority-stake strategy. The IRS prevails on the transfer-pricing method, so beyond the bridge deduction the forward cash tax rate rises to 24% as royalty income is taxed in the US and the Swiss incentive lapses. Terminal growth 2%.

base.narrative: TAVR (74%) grows 7-8% in 2027-28 on the asymptomatic indication and the Sep-2026 CMS NCD, fading to 4-5% as the core US/EU markets mature and share slips slightly to Evolut; Surgical (17%) grows 3-4%; TMTT (11.5%) compounds ~30% -> 15% -> 10%, reaching ~$1.6B by 2030, the low-middle of the $1.5-2.0B target. Blended growth 9.5% decelerating to 3.5%. EBITDA margin expands 2.5pp over the decade as TMTT reaches scale profitability, net of a permanent ~1.5pp litigation/external-innovation drag. Cash tax ramps 18% -> 22% as the Swiss incentive expires in 2032. Capex intensity drifts 4.2% -> 3.5% as the manufacturing build completes; D&A catches up toward it. Working capital absorbs 15% of each year's revenue increase (receivables ~75 days, tissue-valve inventory ~1 year of COGS).

bull.narrative: The moderate aortic stenosis indication (PROGRESS) is approved around 2028-29 and, with the asymptomatic cohort and under-penetrated Europe/Japan/RoW, keeps TAVR at 9-10% for five years; TMTT reaches the top of the $1.5-2.0B 2030 target as EVOQUE, PASCAL and SAPIEN M3 become the standard full mitral/tricuspid portfolio against Abbott; Surgical holds mid-single digits on RESILIA. Operating leverage on a 78-79% gross margin takes the EBITDA margin to 37%. The IRS dispute settles near the bridge expectation and the Swiss incentive is partly replaced, so the cash tax rate tops out at 20%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: management itself now frames TAVR growth as volume-led with a 'slight long-term share loss', the July-2024 guidance cut shows how fast a capacity-driven miss reprices the stock, and the IRS transfer-pricing dispute is an open-ended, escalating tail (penalties asserted Q3-2026) only partly captured by the bridge. Bull cut to 25%: it needs three independent things -- PROGRESS approval with no timeline yet given, TMTT at the top of its 2030 range, and TAVR holding 9-10% despite acknowledged competitive share erosion. No live corporate action, so the three-scenario frame holds.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
